Content Quality.definition: Grammar, word choice, clarity of ideas, and overall language proficiency in the written script.

guidelines.1: Poor grammar with frequent errors, unclear word choices, and confusing ideas. Language is inappropriate or unprofessional.
guidelines.2: Noticeable grammar errors and awkward word choices. Ideas are somewhat unclear or poorly expressed.
guidelines.3: Generally good grammar and word choice with occasional errors. Ideas are mostly clear and well-expressed.
guidelines.4: Strong grammar and excellent word choice. Ideas are clear, well-articulated, and professionally expressed.
guidelines.5: Exceptional grammar and sophisticated word choice. Ideas are crystal clear, eloquently expressed, and demonstrate mastery.

Structure & Organization.definition: Logical flow, coherent organization, effective transitions, and overall structural soundness of the script.

guidelines.1: No clear structure or organization. Ideas jump randomly without logical connections or transitions.
guidelines.2: Poor organization with weak transitions. Structure is difficult to follow and lacks coherence.
guidelines.3: Basic organization with some logical flow. Transitions are present but may be awkward or unclear.
guidelines.4: Well-organized with clear structure and smooth transitions. Ideas flow logically from one to the next.
guidelines.5: Exceptionally organized with masterful structure. Seamless transitions create perfect logical flow.

Professionalism & Tone.definition: Appropriateness of language, tone, and style for the intended audience and presentation context.

guidelines.1: Completely inappropriate tone or language for the audience. Unprofessional or offensive content.
guidelines.2: Mostly inappropriate tone with frequent lapses in professionalism. Language doesn't match audience expectations.
guidelines.3: Generally appropriate tone with occasional informal language. Mostly suitable for the intended audience.
guidelines.4: Professional and appropriate tone throughout. Language perfectly matches audience and context expectations.
guidelines.5: Exceptionally professional with masterful tone adaptation. Language demonstrates sophisticated audience awareness.

Engagement Potential.definition: How compelling, interesting, and engaging the written content would be when delivered to the target audience.

guidelines.1: Content is completely unengaging, boring, or irrelevant. No attempt to capture audience interest.
guidelines.2: Content lacks engagement with minimal interesting elements. Little consideration for audience interest.
guidelines.3: Content has some engaging elements but inconsistent appeal. Moderate consideration for audience engagement.
guidelines.4: Content is engaging and interesting with compelling elements. Strong consideration for audience appeal.
guidelines.5: Content is exceptionally engaging and captivating. Masterful use of compelling elements to maintain interest.

Delivery Readiness.definition: How well the script is prepared for oral delivery, including readability, natural speech patterns, and speaking cues.

guidelines.1: Script is extremely difficult to read aloud with unnatural language and no consideration for oral delivery.
guidelines.2: Script is challenging to deliver with awkward phrasing and poor readability for speaking.
guidelines.3: Script is moderately ready for delivery with some natural language but occasional awkward phrases.
guidelines.4: Script flows naturally when spoken with good readability and speech-friendly language.
guidelines.5: Script is perfectly crafted for oral delivery with natural speech patterns and excellent flow when spoken.
